parts.title: Strange Loops, Meaning, and GEB's Evolution

sentences: Inanimate matter can create **animate beings** through **strange loops**, which are **swirly, twisty, vortex-like patterns**.
M.C. Escher's art shows these **strange loops**, and the **inspiration** for this idea came from **Kurt Gödel's incompleteness theorem**.
**Gödel's strange loop** lets mathematical systems **"perceive themselves"** and become **"self-aware"** from **meaningless symbols**.
**Meaning** arises when patterns **accurately track** things in the world.
The author believes **complex self-mirroring patterns** in brains create **strange loops of consciousness**.
**Strange loops** are the mark of a **self**, connecting inanimate to animate.
A **"twisted loop of selfhood"** in a brain has **causal power**.
An **"I"** forms when brain patterns mirror themselves, like a **TV camera pointed at a TV screen**.
The dialogue between the **Author** and **God** became the **"Six-part Ricercar"** in **GEB**.
Translating **GEB** into other languages offered a chance to address the **sexist sin** of the original.
Translations faced challenges due to **wordplay** and **"structural puns"**.
The author spent a year annotating **GEB** for translators.
A key challenge was translating **"Mr. Tortoise"** into **French** because the noun **tortue** is feminine.
The author **unthinkingly** assumed the **Tortoise** was male, showing how **sexism** can subtly pervade thinking.
**Jacqueline Henry** and **Bob French** changed the **Tortoise's sex** to **female**, resulting in **"Madame Tortue"**.
This felt faithful to **Carroll's** sexually neutral **tortoise**, and **Italian** translators followed suit.

parts.title: From Formal Systems to Paradoxes: A Journey of Thought

sentences: This book was conceived over nearly **twenty years**, starting when the author was **thirteen years** old.
An early fascination was taking **three 3's** and operating on **3 with itself**.
The author's **parents** were **pillars of support**, **guided**, **inspired**, **encouraged**, and **sustained** him.
This book is **dedicated** to them.
Friends Robert Boeninger and Peter Jones helped **mold ways of thought**, and Charles Brenner taught programming.
**Ernest Nagel** was a **long-time friend** and **mentor**.
Scott Kim exerted a **gigantic influence** through his **art**, **music**, and **new perspectives**.
Don Byrd knew the book **forwards and backwards** and provided **good ideas**.
In the **nineteenth century**, logicians codified **deductive reasoning** patterns.
**Gottlob Frege**, **Giuseppe Peano**, and **David Hilbert** worked to clarify the meaning of "**proof**".
**Georg Cantor** developed **set theory**, introducing **different types of infinities**.
This **powerful and beautiful** theory led to **set-theoretical paradoxes** which were **disturbing**.
The **most famous paradox** is **Russell's paradox**, concerning whether a **set contains itself**.
The paradox arises when considering "R: the set of all run-of-the-mill sets."
These paradoxes share a common culprit: **self-reference**, or "**Strange Loopiness**."
**Russell and Whitehead's** _Principia Mathematica_ aimed to eliminate these loops using a **theory of types**.
This theory created a **hierarchy of sets** but was seen as an "**overkill**" that sacrificed **interesting complexity**.
A **decision procedure** determines if a string is a **theorem** in a formal system.
It is **guaranteed to terminate**.
This provides **certitude** for theoremhood, unlike the **MIU-system**.
The **pq-system** exemplifies formal systems using 'p', 'q', and **hyphens**.
It has an **infinite number of axioms** and one **production rule**.
A **decision procedure** for its theorems determines if the lengths of the first two hyphen-groups sum to the third, a property preserved by the rule.
Formal systems can capture **addition** and **multiplication**.
The **tq-system** represents multiplication where **X times Y equals Z** by using hyphens.
A **composite number** of hyphens for Z means a C-system theorem if **x-ty-qz** is a theorem.
A rule stating "if **Cx** is not a theorem, then **Px** is a theorem" is flawed.
This is because checking for non-theorems is not a **typographical operation**.
Formal systems need **explicit typographical rules**.
The C-system's non-theorems, which have a **prime number** of hyphens, are **negatively defined**.

parts.title: Contracrostipunctus and the Little Harmonic Labyrinth

sentences: The **Contracrostipunctus** illustrates its own themes of **backfirings**, with its design mirroring the events it shows.
Each part of the **Contracrostipunctus** is like a copy of **Gödel's Theorem**, using two levels of meaning in number theory.

The connection between the **Contracrostipunctus** and **Gödel's Theorem** involves concepts where a **phonograph** acts like an **axiomatic system** and a **record** is like a **string** in that system.
For instance, a song title "I Cannot Be Played on Record Player X" maps to "I Cannot Be Derived in Formal System X", showing their **isomorphism**.
**Consistency** means every **theorem** is a **true statement** when interpreted.
**Completeness** means every **true statement** in the system's notation is a **theorem**.
A system can be **consistent** but **incomplete**, where **symbols** and their **interpretations** do not fully match.
The **modified pq-system** is an example, being **consistent** but **incomplete**.
To achieve both, one might **tighten the interpretation** or **add new rules**.
The Tortoise and Achilles drink **pushing-potion** to enter **Escher's Convex and Concave**, using a **gondola**.
**Escher pictures are connected**, allowing travel between them.
Achilles grabs a **magic copper lamp** guarded by **lizards**, who turn mortals into pickles, and is left **dangling**.
A **boy** rescues Achilles, puts the lizards to sleep, and Achilles gets the lamp.
The lamp contains a **genie**, and Achilles wishes for **a hundred wishes**, but the Genie calls this a **meta-wish**.
A **recursive chain of djinns** is summoned by a **Meta-Genie** and **Meta-Meta-Genie** from nested lamps.
This defines **GOD** as **"GOD Over Djinn"**, a hierarchy of djinns.
Achilles uses his **Typeless Wish** to wish for his wish **not to be granted**, causing a **paradox** that makes the **"System crash"**.
They are transported to **Tumbolia**, then reappear in Escher's **Reptiles** picture.
They enter the **Little Harmonic Labyrinth**, a **Bach organ piece** with musical grooves.
The **Majotaur** laughs victims to death.
They **pop** back to normal size and out of the labyrinth after eating what they hope is popcorn.
Lizards can exit pictures by moving **perpendicularly** to the plane, a method they use to return to the Tortoise's house.
A **recursive definition** uses **simpler versions** of itself to define something, which avoids **infinite regress**.
Recursion is like **nesting** stories or Russian dolls.
Computer scientists use **push**, **pop**, and **stack** to describe recursion.
To **push** means suspending a task to start a new, **lower-level** one.
To **pop** means finishing a task and resuming the one left off, one level higher.
A **stack** stores information like **return addresses**.
News reports use recursion when reporters switch to correspondents.
In music, listeners have a **mental stack of keys**, expecting **reverse order retracing** back to the tonic.
Bach's **Little Harmonic Labyrinth** disorients listeners with **quick key changes**.
Language uses **push-down stacks** for grammar, like the German **verb-at-the-end**.
**Recursive Transition Networks (RTNs)** use diagrams of **nodes** and **arcs** to describe recursive structures.
**True recursion** in RTNs is when an RTN calls itself, such as **FANCY NOUN** calling **FANCY NOUN**.
Recursion avoids **infinite regress** because at least one pathway **avoids self-reference** and can **bottom out**.
Music can have **nested loops**, like a **scale** played with **pitch displacement**.
Prokofiev and Rachmaninoff use **fast, medium, and slow scale-loops** played **simultaneously**.
A **subroutine** or **procedure** is a group of operations treated as a **single unit with a name**.
Procedures can **call each other by name**, creating **concise sequences of operations** and **modularity**.
Modularity is found in **hierarchically organized systems**.
Procedures often need to act **variably based on context**, using **memory** or **parameters**.
When an RTN adds **parameters and conditions**, it becomes an **Augmented Transition Network (ATN)**.
ATNs can generate **sensible English sentences** using **semantic constraints**.
Choosing the **"best" chess move** is a recursive procedure with parameters.
Evaluating a move involves pretending it's made and assessing the board from the **opponent's perspective**.
The **recursive definition of "best move"** can go **several levels deep**.
It **bottoms out** by evaluating board positions without further look-ahead, using criteria like **number of pieces**.
A **look-ahead parameter** decreases with each recursive call, leading to a **non-recursive evaluation** when zero.
Game-playing programs create a **"look-ahead tree"**.
**Hofstadter's Law** states tasks always take longer than expected, even when accounting for the law itself, suggesting **recursive unpredictability**.

The concept of **meaning** may depend on the **type of intelligence** perceiving it. To define intelligence beyond human views, **independent characteristics** are needed. Progress in cognitive psychology, AI, and neuroscience may synthesize an **objective definition of intelligence**, even if human-centric. This definition could characterize the **essence of intelligence** abstractly, reducing anthropocentric bias. Contact with an **alien civilization** would suggest human intelligence is not a fluke, implying meaning could be an **inherent property**.

A **rectangular plaque** with **two dots** cannot effectively convey meaning. A second plaque with a **sequence of dots** representing **Fibonacci numbers** reveals a rule. This **"long genotype"** provides enough information to infer the underlying recursive rule. **"Short genotypes"** are triggers, assuming the rule is already built into the intelligence. The **clarity of an outer message** depends on its length.

Using **derived rules** in **Propositional Calculus** speeds up derivations but **sacrifices formality** because these rules are derived **informally**. Formal systems were created for **every explicit step** of a proof to be **mechanically checked**. Abandoning this for **shortcuts** defeats the system's purpose. Formalizing the metatheory makes **derived rules** into **theorems** of a larger system, legitimizing their use. This leads to the idea of **metametatheories**, implying that **shortcuts** will always be sought at the highest level. Distinguishing between **working in the system** (M-mode) and **thinking about the system** (I-mode) is crucial. Assuming that **symbols** can be freely exchanged between the formal system's language and its **metalanguage** is a **dangerous practice**.

parts.title: TNT Axioms, Zen, Escher, and the MIU-System

sentences: The **five axioms of TNT** concern the number **0** and the operations of **addition** and **multiplication**.
These are similar to **Peano's five postulates** for natural numbers from **1889**.
Peano's postulates use "djinn" for natural numbers, with "Genie" and "meta" as other undefined terms.
**Genie is a djinn**, and every djinn has a **meta** that is also a djinn.
**Genie is not the meta** of any djinn, and **different djinns have different metas**.
The fifth postulate, or **principle of mathematical induction**, states that if Genie has property X and every djinn relays X to its meta, then **all djinns get X**.
The **Rule of Specification** allows dropping a **universal quantifier** and replacing the variable with a term, if the term does not contain a quantified variable.
The **Rule of Generalization** adds a **universal quantifier** to a theorem with a free variable.
The **Rule of Interchange** permits swapping universal and existential quantifiers, such as "Va:~" and "~∃a:".
The **Rule of Existence** replaces terms in a theorem with a new variable and adds an **existential quantifier**.
Rules for **Equality** include **Symmetry** and **Transitivity**.
Rules for **Successorship** include **Add S** and **Drop S**.
Zen **koans** are designed to **bewilder** and encourage **nonlogical** thought, moving beyond **dualism**.
Dualism is the conceptual and **perceptual division** of the world into **categories**, with **words** at its core.
Zen opposes **reliance on words** because they are inherently dualistic.
The goal is to suppress **perception** and **logical, verbal thinking**, leading to an **Un-mode** of being.
Zen emphasizes **holism**, suggesting the world cannot be divided into parts, and the **borderlines between self and universe** should dissolve.
The Zen monk **Bassui** describes this as a snowflake melting, its essence remaining in **Tumbolia**.
Zen acknowledges its **limitations**, similar to mathematicians recognizing limits of **axiomatic methods** for truth.
**M.C. Escher's art**, with its contradictory images, shares a spirit with Zen by **breaking the mind of logic**.
Escher's work, like **Day and Night** or **Three Spheres II**, explores **interconnectedness** and **unity in opposition**.
The **MIU-system** can be applied to **number theory**.
The **I-count** (number of 'I's) in MIU theorems is never zero and never a **multiple of 3**.
Rules **I and IV** do not change the I-count.
Rule **III** reduces the I-count by **3**, and rule **II** doubles it.

parts.title: MU-Puzzle, Godel-Numbering, and Levels of Description

sentences: The **I-count** cannot become a **multiple of 3** because the **MIU-system rules** never create one from the starting **I-count** of **1**.
Therefore, **MU** is **not a theorem** of the **MIU-system**.
This **MU-puzzle** was solved using a **simple number-theoretical argument**.
A **Godel-numbering** embeds **formal system problems**, like the **MIU-system**, into **number theory** using an **isomorphism**.
Each **MIU-system** symbol maps to a **number**: **M** to **3**, **I** to **1**, and **U** to **0**.
A multiletter string's **Godel number** is formed by concatenating the **Cadet numbers** of its symbols.
This mapping is an **information-preserving transformation**.
A **derivation** can be represented in both **typographical** and **numerical notations**, with the **numerical representation** having a **dual nature**.
**GODEL'S STRING G** and a **Bach fugue** can be understood on **different levels**.
Humans can be described by **trillions of cells** or **molecules**.
We accept these **different pictures** by **disconnecting them** and **storing separate representations**.
We rarely compare these **different concepts**.
A **major problem** in **Artificial Intelligence** is bridging the gap between **different descriptions**.
Progress in **computer chess** shows this challenge, as early attempts focused on **looking further ahead**.
Studies show **chess masters perceive patterns** as **chunks**, unlike novices.
Masters quickly reproduce board positions, indicating a **higher-level mental image** and sensitivity to **recurring patterns**.
A **gas** obeys precise, deterministic laws due to **canceling effects**.
These **chunked laws** treat the gas as a **whole**.
The **microscopic** and **macroscopic** gas descriptions use entirely different terms.
The law **pV = cT** relates temperature, pressure, and volume.
High-level laws cannot be stated in **low-level vocabulary**.
**Pressure** and **temperature** are new terms.
**Epiphenomena** are visible consequences of overall system organization.
A computer's performance degradation at 35 users is an **epiphenomenon**.
A sprinter's 9.3-second time is a result of interacting factors, not a stored number.
In the **human brain**, **gullibility** is an epiphenomenon.
The text questions if **consciousness** is an epiphenomenon.
**Computers** create "thinking" machines, offering new perspectives on **thought**.
This shows human thought's **idiosyncrasies**, weaknesses, and powers.
**Thought** needs representing reality in the brain.
The brain uses **active symbols** with rules mixed in.
A **calculus of descriptions** is central to thinking.
**Neurons** decide to fire if inputs exceed a threshold.
**Larger structures** of neurons likely handle concepts.
Memories might be **coded locally but redundantly**.
The idea of a single "**grandmother cell**" for complex concepts is not accepted.
The brain has a **columnar organization** in the visual cortex.
**Modules** (neural complexes) are hypothesized for each concept.
These **symbols** can be dormant or active.
Thinking involves **classes** and **instances**.
New symbols can form when unlinked symbols activate consistently.
To count symbols in a brain, one would need to include all **dormant symbols**.
The existence of "potential symbols" shows that viewing the brain as a collection of symbols in well-defined states is an **oversimplification**.
Symbol **overlapping** is probably the rule, with each neuron potentially functioning as part of **hundreds of symbols**.
A theory based on symbols can still work even if they **physically overlap**, like different waves on a **pond's surface**.
Distinguishing symbol activations might involve identifying the **precise timing** of their firing.
Artificial Intelligence suggests intelligence can be realized in **different hardware**, making it a **software property**.
This implies consciousness and intelligence are **high-level phenomena** with their own laws, separable from lower levels, a concept referred to as **"liftability"**.
Translating broken Russian with a German accent into English is challenging.
Using an **analogous phrase** risks a "Campbell's soup" blunder, while a word-by-word translation sounds **alien**.
Warren Weaver suggested that a Russian article is "really written in English, but it has been coded in some strange symbols."
Weaver's remark implies there is an **objectively describable meaning** hidden in symbols that a well-programmed computer could **decode**.
Comparing programs requires determining the correct **level of comparison**.
A **higher, more chunked view** is needed to perceive **chunks of program** that show the programmer's goals.
An **abstract "conceptual skeleton"** must be extracted from low levels for a **meaningful comparison** of programs.
A **BlooP** procedure has one input **parameter** and uses **block structure**, where portions are **units**.
Each block has a **number** and is delimited by **BEGIN** and **END**.
A **LOOP** statement executes a block repeatedly, and blocks can be **nested**.
The **algorithm** calculates 2^(3N), using **CELL(0)** multiplied by 3 **N times**, and **CELL(1)** multiplied by 2 **CELL(0)** times.
The **OUTPUT** variable stores the **value**, defaulting to **0** at the start.
BlooP has **IF-statements** and **branching**.
The **MINUS** procedure subtracts **N** from **M**; if **M < N**, it **QUITS BLOCK 0**, resulting in **0**.
Otherwise, it increments **OUTPUT** in **LOOP 1** until **OUTPUT + N = M**, then **ABORTS LOOP 1**.
**QUIT** pertains to **blocks**, while **ABORT** pertains to **loops**.
**QUIT BLOCK n** jumps to the **last line** of **BLOCK n**, and **ABORT LOOP n** jumps just **below** the **last line** of **BLOCK n**.
The **AT MOST** keyword indicates a loop may be **aborted early**.
Once defined, a procedure can be called in **later definitions**.
Some **BlooP procedures** can output **YES** or **NO** as **tests**, with names ending in a **question mark** and **OUTPUT** defaulting to **NO**.
The **Church-Turing Thesis** suggests that what is **human-computable is also FlooP-computable**.
FlooP-computable functions are either **general recursive** (terminating) or **partial recursive** (non-terminating).

A **proof-pair** translates TNT statements into **number theory**, consisting of two natural numbers: the **Godel number of a TNT derivation** and the **Godel number of the derivation's bottom line**.
This proof-pair property is **primitive recursive** and **representable in TNT** by a formula.
The **substitution relationship** is also **primitive recursive** and **representable in TNT**.
The **incompleteness of TNT** is shown by string G, which states "**G is not a theorem of TNT**".
If G is a TNT-theorem, it creates a **contradiction**.
If G is a nontheorem, then a **true statement is not provable in TNT**.
TNT cannot prove its own **consistency**; if it could, it would be **inconsistent**.
TNT is **w-incomplete**, meaning a **summarizing string is a nontheorem**, while an **infinite family of related true strings are theorems**.

parts.title: Supernatural Numbers, Self-Reproducing Systems, and Art

sentences: The string "-G" asserts a **truth** in one number theory context, while "G" asserts a **falsity** in another.
In **standard number theory**, the opposite is true, and no **supernatural numbers** exist.
A **supernatural theorem** in **TNT** may assert a falsity, but all **natural theorems** still assert truths.
Supernaturals are indexed by a trio of **ordinary integers**.
It is possible to calculate the index for the **sum** of two supernaturals under some **indexing schemes**, or for their **product** under others.
No **single indexing scheme** allows for the recursive calculation of both **sum** and **product** indices.
Nonstandard analysis, using **supernatural real numbers** and **infinitesimals**, can provide a new foundation for **calculus** and more intuitive proofs.
The question of which **number theory** is "correct" is difficult because different theories use the same terms but refer to **different concepts**.
The meanings of terms like "number" are defined by the **axiomatic system** they are used in.
Achilles notes that **Rene Magritte** and **M.C. Escher** both use **realism to explore paradox and illusion**, have **visual symbols**, and possess **graceful lines**.
Crab shows a painting that depicts a **normal pipe with a tiny tree**, not a giant pipe with a tree.
Crab removes the pipe from the painting, revealing it to be real, and smokes it.
He recites Bach's poem, "Edifying Thoughts of a Tobacco Smoker," which compares **life and death to a pipe's existence**.
Crab plays a record on his **Tortoise-chomping record player**, designed to **destroy records made by Mr. Tortoise**.
Mr. Tortoise's records previously targeted a **stable disassembly-reassembly subunit** in Crab's phonographs.
Crab learned about **"spontaneous self-assembly"** hoping to create an indestructible phonograph, but this failed due to something like "Godel's Theorem."
He now aims for a **survivable phonograph** that only plays his records using a **labeling technique** and **style-screening process**.

parts.title: Typogenetics, Real Genetics, and Biological Parallels

sentences: **Typogenetics** uses special **enzymes** on **strands** of letters.
Each enzyme has **three-letter operations** and binds to a preferred letter.
Enzymes **quit** if they move off a strand.
Some enzymes search for **pyrimidines** or **purines** and enter "Copy mode".
In **Copy mode**, letters copy onto another strand as **complementary bases**.
The **two complementary strands** then separate to create new ones.
The **Typogenetic Code** translates **duplets** into amino acids.
**Ribosomes** read strands and produce coded enzymes.
An enzyme's **tertiary structure** determines its **binding preference**.
**Real genetics** uses **DNA** made of **adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), or thymine (T)**.
DNA forms a **double strand** where A pairs with T, and C pairs with G.
**Messenger RNA (mRNA)** carries genetic information from **DNA** to **ribosomes**.
**Ribosomes** create **proteins** by translating mRNA sequences.
The **Genetic Code** translates **triplets of nucleotides** into amino acids.
A protein's **tertiary structure** determines its function.
The **Central Dogma** shows how strands define enzymes, and enzymes act on strands.
The **Central Dogmap** shows **mathematical logic** and **molecular biology** share an **abstract structure**.
Both systems have **"loops"** of complexity, where **proteins** act on other proteins, and **statements** are about other statements.
An **Immunity Theorem** in molecular biology is like **Gödel's Theorem**.
It says you can design a **DNA strand** a cell cannot reproduce, possibly causing the cell to **destroy itself**.
**Viruses** are like "Henkin sentences"; **self-assembling viruses** are implicit.
**Complex viruses** are explicit, coding for enzymes to direct their assembly.
**Cellular differentiation** and **morphogenesis** are key biological problems involving **feedback** and **feedforward mechanisms**.
Cells regulate protein production by **inhibition** or **repression** using **repressors**.
**Inducers** can counteract repressors to allow gene expression.
The **Church-Turing Thesis** suggests any number-sorting method can be described by a **FlooP program**.
The **Church-Turing Thesis** is a **hypothesis** about how **human brains** process information.

The **Public-Processes Version** states that if a **sentient being** uses a method that always gives a **finite-time answer** and can be **communicated reliably**, then a **terminating FlooP program** gives the **same answers**.
This suggests **public methods** can be "FlooPified" but makes **no claims** about **private methods**.
The **Isomorphism Version** claims a sentient being's **mental processes** can be **isomorphically mirrored** in a **FlooP program** at some level.
The **Microscopic Version** suggests **living components' behavior** can be **simulated by a computer**.
The **Reductionist's Version** states **all brain processes** come from a **computable substrate**, supporting **Artificial Intelligence**.
SHRDLU handles **logical connectives** like "and" and "or" using its **grammar** and **semantics**.
It understands words like "littlest" by interpreting their **root forms**.
SHRDLU asks for **clarification** on "on top of" when **disambiguation heuristics** are not clear.
It deduces events from its **memory** and relates them in **time**, understanding **complex tenses**.
SHRDLU remembers **immediately previous sentences** to answer questions like "why?" and understands its own motives by tracking **subgoal trees**.
It checks statements about **basic object properties** and **location** against its complete information.
SHRDLU understands syntactically ambiguous commands by choosing the interpretation that makes **sense in the current scene**.

parts.title: AI: Problem Solving and Knowledge Representation

sentences: A **tree-like structure** of subgoals for problem-solving does not always guarantee a resolution if **knowledge is unavailable**.
Such a system might respond with "I do not know," like the **incompleteness** in some formal systems.
This **deductive awareness** allows logical conclusions but lacks **analogical awareness**, which spots similarities.
Early logic systems did not capture **analogical thought**, though modern systems allow **complex comparisons**.
Representing knowledge is different from storing numbers; a computer's "memory" is not what it "knows" without **access procedures**.
Knowledge can be **inaccessible** or "forgotten" at a high level, even if present at a low level, depending on how experiences are stored.
The **complexity of human knowledge representation** became clear while developing a program to **generate English sentences**.
The goal was to program **creative acts**, inspired by "Computer Haiku."
A **flexible and recursive grammar** was created, leading to a Recursive Transition Network (RTN) grammar.
Word selection started randomly with the **overall sentence structure** and went down to word and letter levels.
Early versions produced **humorous nonsense sentences** with complex structures.
The output became stale as its **limits of behavior space** became apparent.
Achieving truly humorous output needed more **subtlety**, using words in line with **real-world realities**, which introduced **knowledge representation**.
In Bongard problems, creating a **template** is challenging due to **variety**, needing **higher-level abstraction**.
The program uses **meta-descriptions**, which describe descriptions, to identify **common features**.
For example, in BP 91, the meta-description of box I-E shows "**3 copies**" of a specific line segment as a **recurring concept**.
A **sameness-detector** then identifies "**three-ness**" for Class I boxes and "**four-ness**" for Class II boxes by checking meta-descriptions.
This **meta-description** approach provides **flexibility** for solving problems in different ways.
When **preprocessing** shows too much diversity, it means **higher-level concepts** are involved.
**Throwing away information** involves **focusing** on parts of a drawing and **filtering** out all but certain concepts.
Inspecting a **simple box** helps in **discovering features** for template building.

parts.title: AI, Free Will, and the Sloth Canon

sentences: AI programs will likely have **greater differences** from people than people do from each other.
An AI's **"body"** would give it **different perspectives**.
An understandable AI program would likely seem **alien**, making it hard to tell from a **"weird" program**.
Humans likely have the best possible **intuitive understanding** of intelligence, consciousness, and free will, similar to how one appreciates music.
Achilles and the Tortoise discuss Zeno's paradox and a race where Achilles **could not catch up**.
Achilles plays a "sloth-piano" with **inverted melodies**, like **sloths** who do things about **half as fast**.
Bach's "Canon per augmentationem, contrario motu" also has **slowed-down and inverted** melodies, with the letters "SAT" preceding the staves.
This is called the **"Sloth Canon"**.
A **marble rolling down a bumpy hill** does not make choices, even if its path is **unpredictable**.
Calculators or chess programs are like "fancy marbles" because their outcomes are **repeatable**.
These programs lack **self-awareness** and do not have a sense of free will.
A robot in a T-maze making choices based on the square root of 2's digits **models the situation with symbols**.
The robot does not know its next turn, as its decider is a **black box** to it.
The robot does not make choices if its mind does not **affect the outcome**.
When a robot's **self-symbol** affects its decisions, it resembles human choice, and **meaning enters the picture**.
Qualities like "**will**," "**intuition**," and "**consciousness**" can emerge from such programs.
This balance between **self-knowledge and self-ignorance** creates the feeling of free will.
A system is a "**choice maker**" when we can identify with its **high-level description**.

parts.title: Bibliography: Key Works in Artificial Intelligence and Related Fields

sentences: A **bibliography** includes asterisks indicating **prime motivators** (two asterisks) or **special features/quirks** (one asterisk) of a book.
Instead of **direct pointers** to **technical literature**, the bibliography offers **meta-pointers** to books that contain such pointers.
**John Allen's The Anatomy of LISP** is the **most comprehensive book on LISP**, a **computer language** that dominated **Artificial Intelligence research** for two decades.
**Margaret Boden's Artificial Intelligence and Natural Man** is the **best book** on **AI aspects**, covering both **technical** and **philosophical questions**.
It is known for its **clear thinking** and **extensive technical bibliography**.
Her other book, **Purposive Explanation in Psychology**, is considered an **extended footnote** to the AI book.
